title: Pairs at the Smallest Gap
statement:
You get an array nums of distinct integers. The gap between two values is the larger one minus the smaller one.

Find the smallest gap between any two values in the array, and return every pair that has exactly that gap. Write each pair as [a, b] with a < b, and list the pairs in increasing order of a.

examples.why: Sorted, the values are 1, 4, 7, 10. Every neighbouring gap is 3, so all three pairs tie.
The gaps after sorting are 2, 6 and 3. The closest pair is not next to each other in the input.
Two separate pairs both have gap 2. Report both, smaller a first.

hints: Comparing every pair is O(n²). Is there an order in which the closest pairs are easy to find?
After sorting, the closest value to any element is one of its neighbours. So the smallest gap is between two neighbours.
Sort, then do one pass to find the smallest neighbouring gap and a second pass (or the same pass, resetting a list) to collect every neighbouring pair with that gap.

explain.intuition:
If a < b < c in sorted order, then c − a is bigger than both b − a and c − b. So a pair that skips over a value can never have the smallest gap. Only neighbours in sorted order are candidates, and there are just n − 1 of them.

Sorting also gives the output order for free: walking neighbours left to right lists the pairs in increasing order of a.
steps: Walk neighbours (nums[i − 1], nums[i]) and track the smallest gap best along with a result list.
If the gap is smaller than best, set best to it and reset the list to just this pair.
If the gap equals best, add the pair to the list.
pitfalls: Sorting with the default JavaScript sort(), which compares as strings: [-3, -1, 10, 5] ends up in the wrong order. Pass (a, b) => a − b.
Keeping only the first pair with the smallest gap. Ties are common and all of them must be returned.
Forgetting to clear the collected pairs when a strictly smaller gap appears.

complexity.space: O(n) for the sorted copy and the output

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: Compute the gap of every pair, keep the pairs with the smallest gap, then sort them.

solutions.title: Sort, then compare neighbours
solutions.idea: After sorting, only neighbours can be closest. One pass finds the smallest gap and collects every neighbouring pair with it.

followups: The values fit in a small range, say 0 to 1 000 000. Can you avoid the comparison sort?
Values may now repeat. What is the smallest gap, and how should duplicate pairs be reported?
